  {"question": "According to arXiv 2508.06411, what are the three levels of the AI value chain where risk management should be implemented, and which references support each level?", "answer": "Risk management should be implemented at the model level ([67]), the system or application level ([149]), and the broader societal and political level ([150], [151]).", "evidence": [{"page": 16, "quote": "It is crucial to conduct risk management at all levels of the value chain, which includes:

· The model level, e.g. during data collection, training, post-training, or deployment [67].

· The system or application level i.e. the specific areas it is being used [149]

· Broader societal and political level [150], [151]"}, {"page": 24, "quote": "[149] Jia Yi Goh et al. Measuring What Matters: A Framework for Evaluating Safety Risks in Real-World LLM Applications. 2025. arXiv: 2507.09820 [cs.SE]. URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09820.

[150] Nestor Maslej et al. Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2025. Tech. rep. [Accessed: 29 July 2025]. Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, Apr. 2025. URL: https://hai.stanford.edu/aiindex/2025-ai-index-report.

[151] Jamie Bernardi et al. Societal Adaptation to Advanced AI. 2025. arXiv: 2405.10295 [cs.CY]. URL: https: //arxiv.org/abs/2405.10295."}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2508.06411, what are the four key areas suggested for future research on catastrophic AI risk management?", "answer": "The four areas are: open-ended risk exploration, developing comprehensive risk pathway models, quantifying risks, and investigating mitigation measures beyond model and application levels.", "evidence": [{"page": 16, "quote": "Future research can focus on four key areas. First, risks can be identified by conducting open-ended exploration across various risk dimensions. Second, more comprehensive risk pathway models can be developed, incorporating a wider array of scenarios and detailed mitigation strategies. Third, risks can be quantified by estimating the probability and severity based on its pathways and the effectiveness of proposed mitigations. Lastly, further investigation into risk mitigation measures beyond the model and application level, at the application and societal level, would be beneficial for managing these risks holistically."}]},
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2508.06411, which organization funded the research and which initiative provided coworking space support?", "answer": "The research was funded by the Open Philanthropy AI Governance and Policy grant and supported by LISA (London Initiative for Safe AI) through subsidized coworking space.", "evidence": [{"page": 16, "quote": "This work was funded by the Open Philanthropy AI Governance and Policy grant, and supported by LISA (London Initiative for Safe AI) through subsidized access to its research coworking space."}]},
